business_problem: TriZetto needed to migrate mission-critical healthcare databases to the cloud without sacrificing HIPAA compliance, but self-managing on-premises MongoDB and other platforms was consuming engineering time that the company needed for innovation.
solution_summary: TriZetto modernized its healthcare data platform by moving key workloads from self-managed MongoDB Enterprise Advanced and other databases onto MongoDB Atlas. The migration was handled incrementally: the team first proved Atlas on part of one product, expanded to a second, and then established Atlas as the default target for new unstructured-data workloads. Atlas removed the operational burden of patching, replication, and disaster-recovery management while still meeting the strict security, redundancy, and high-availability requirements imposed by HIPAA-regulated workloads. MongoDB's engineers also supported the rollout with training and working sessions across TriZetto offices, which helped the company evaluate Atlas against competing hyperscaler and legacy options. As a result, TriZetto turned database modernization into a repeatable cloud-migration pattern that improves performance while freeing teams to focus on product and regulatory change.

solution_components.name: MongoDB Atlas
solution_components.role: Provides the managed cloud database platform that now runs TriZetto's modernized healthcare workloads.

data_flow: Healthcare data that previously lived in self-managed MongoDB and other databases is migrated onto MongoDB Atlas, where managed replication, availability, and security support application workloads such as Unify and Connected Health without the former operational overhead.
business_outcome: TriZetto cut latency and manual work, reduced costs, and gave its business units a cloud-ready database foundation that can adapt faster to regulatory and market change.
